subject: GrowthPilot pilot: throughput sketch and next-step asks
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@growthpilot.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: GrowthPilot pilot: throughput sketch and next-step asks

Samir — great talk today, thanks for walking through the GrowthPilot use case. A short recap focused on the performance/throughput items we promised to follow up on so your engineers can evaluate the pilot quickly.

Key ask: we want to validate a sizing sketch that maps your traffic profile to a Redwood Dedicated pilot config. To do that please send the following artifacts/answers by end of week: 
- Token/QPS distribution sample (CSV or JSON) showing at minimum: timestamp, request_id, token_count, streaming_flag. Sample attached as gp-token-sample.csv with the format we discussed.
- Expected P95 latency target for interactive flows and for async batch flows (in ms). You mentioned ~200-350ms interactive earlier — please confirm per-route.
- Peak vs steady: confirm your 95th/99th percentile qps windows (e.g., 10s peak, 5m sustained). If you don’t have exact windows, approximate peak multiplier vs baseline is fine.
- Concurrency model for streaming sessions: average concurrent streams, average tokens/sec per stream, and whether clients keep sessions open for idle durations (yes/no + idle timeout).
- Any SLO hard constraints (e.g. SLA credit triggers) or acceptable graceful-degradation behaviors (e.g. fallback to smaller model, increased latency).

What Redwood will provide after we ingest your sample: 
- A sizing sketch that shows tokens/sec and GPU counts (reserved pool) under three profiles: baseline, expected peak, stress crest (10x baseline).
- A short runbook for streaming: estimated KV cache hit rates, recommended streaming batch sizes, and latency tradeoffs.
- Cost ballpark and recommended quantization/profile for the pilot.

Attachments: gp-token-sample.csv (format example), redwood-probe-config.json (suggested probe endpoints).

Next step: if you can drop the sample today/tomorrow we’ll turn around the sizing sketch by Tuesday EOD PT.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment: gp-token-sample.csv (CSV sample)
Attachment: redwood-probe-config.json (text)

From: Samir Patel <samir@growthpilot.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: GrowthPilot Platform Team <ops@growthpilot.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:02:15 -0500
Subject: Re: GrowthPilot pilot: throughput sketch and next-step asks

Marcus — thanks for the clear checklist. We attached a reduced sample of last week's request stream (token counts redacted for a public copy, full sample attached to the secure link below). Quick answers inline: 
- P95 targets: interactive routes (chat-like UX): 250ms P95; webhook/async scoring: 1500ms P95.
- Peak windows: our telemetry shows short 15s crests (~6x baseline) and sustained high-load windows of ~7 minutes (~2.2x baseline).
- Streaming concurrency: average concurrent streams 120, typical tokens/sec per stream 20–30 during active typing bursts. Idle sessions stay open ~45s.
- SLO constraints: enterprise customers require 99.9% availability for interactive routes; we can tolerate a fallback to smaller model for non-critical traffic but need explicit rollback within 120s for any model regressions.

We’ve uploaded the full sample to our secure S3 share: https://s3.growthpilot.com/samples/gp-full-token-sample-20260309.csv (internal link). Let me know if you need a different time range or anonymization.

Regards,
Samir
Head of Platform Engineering, GrowthPilot
Attachment: (secure link provided)

Looping in a few ops-focused clarifications so we can size conservatively: 
- For the 15s crest at 6x, confirm whether that crest is correlated across routes (i.e., all interactive routes spike simultaneously) or if it’s concentrated (single route). If correlated, we should plan for the worst-case multiplexing.
- Please ask GrowthPilot whether sessions that report 20–30 tokens/sec have multiple parallel requests per session (multiplexing) or single-stream per client. Multiplexing multiplies KV cache pressure.
- Will GrowthPilot accept a canary rollout that starts 10% traffic for 24 hours then 50% for 6 hours (standard Redwood Dedicated rollout)? Need confirmation because that affects reserved capacity sizing and fallback thresholds.

Also suggested probe plan: run the redwood-probe-config.json config (attached) across 3 AZs for 48 hours to capture crest alignment. Samir — if you can give us access to a small test key we can run it and post the telemetry.

Marissa
Manager, Performance & Reliability | Redwood Inference
Attachment referenced: redwood-probe-config.json

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Thanks Samir — that’s exactly what we needed. Next actions we’ll take: 
1) Redwood to run a sizing sketch based on Samir's sample and Marissa's conservative crest assumptions; deliverable by Tue 2026-03-16 EOD PT.
2) If GrowthPilot can provide a short-lived test key, Redwood will run the probe config for 48h and return probe telemetry and a revised sizing.
3) Confirm rollout plan in writing (Samir): canary 10%/24h -> 50%/6h -> full, yes/no.

We’ll include an appendix showing tokens/sec, estimated GPU slots, and a streaming concurrency table (expected latency tradeoffs at 50/75/95th percentiles).

I’ll bundle the sizing sketch as a single PDF and share the HubSpot deal link after we upload. Thanks all — Marcus

Marcus Lin
